_authority: AUTHORED. Resolution outside an approved path set is refused; membership is tested on the RESOLVED target so a symlink named to look approved does not pass.
_content_binding_note: Content digests are captured at establish() and re-compared at session finish; they are NOT pinned to a repository constant, because the binary differs per runner image and a pinned digest would fail everywhere except where it was generated. This is session-consistent content binding over an approved path set, which is weaker than cryptographic pinning and stronger than path observation. Stated rather than overclaimed.
_derivation: The inventory is DERIVED by scripts/executable_inventory.py from reachable behaviour, not authored. Every derived executable must appear here or the session fails closed. Gate 4N-I28AJ finding ADV-I28AJ-01: the previous policy was only as complete as the person writing it remembered to be.
_dynamic_shell_sites_note: Gate 4N-I28AO. Every command position the model cannot resolve, declared individually with what bounds it. The check is two-way: an undeclared site fails and a stale declaration fails, so neither a new dynamic command nor an obsolete exemption can pass unnoticed.
_dynamic_sites_note: A subprocess whose command word is computed cannot be bounded statically. Each such site is DECLARED here with a reason; an UNDECLARED dynamic site fails closed. Declaring a site makes it visible and reviewable — it does not bind the command, and that limit is stated rather than papered over.
_purpose: Approved locations and trust classification for every external executable the assurance path invokes.

_retired_classifications.REACHABLE_NOT_EXERCISED_IN_GRADED_PATH: RETIRED at Gate 4N-I28AM. It meant 'unbound unless runtime tracing happens to observe it later', and the tracing never ran in a graded session (ADV-I28AL-02). Every executable that carried it is now APPROVED_PATH_SET_AND_CONTENT_BOUND and resolved before graded work.

_why_this_file_exists: Gate 4N-I28AH finding ADV-I28AH-02: git and bash were PATH-discovered and path-recorded but never path-enforced, so a fake binary earlier on PATH was selected while the policy reported clean.

node._i28as: ADDED by Gate 4N-I28AS. npm_authority.resolve_chain() resolves the Node interpreter from the shebang and PATH, which makes `node` a statically reachable executable — and the executable inventory refused the session until it was classified, which is the Gate 4N-I28AJ control working exactly as intended. Its identity is bound as part of the npm chain: canonical path, content digest, object type (a shell script standing in for Node is refused) and the requirement that it belong to the SAME installation as the npm it interprets. It is delegated rather than APPROVED_PATH_SET_AND_CONTENT_BOUND because its authorization is a property of the chain, not of a fixed path list.
node.why_required: npm is a JavaScript entrypoint; the process that actually runs a graded `npm run` step is Node. Binding npm without binding its interpreter would leave the half of the chain that executes the code unbound.

npm._i28ao: RECLASSIFIED from UNREACHABLE_FROM_GRADED_ROOTS. Gate 4N-I28AM chose unreachability to avoid binding a machine-specific version-manager path. Gate 4N-I28AO's command-position derivation, which for the first time reads ci.yml run: blocks, found npm invoked by eight graded steps — so the unreachability claim was FALSE and the precondition that Gate 4N-I28AN found unprotected refuted it as soon as the derivation could see those sites. The precondition worked; the classification did not.
npm._i28as: RECLASSIFIED from APPROVED_PATH_SET_AND_CONTENT_BOUND, and the approved_path_prefixes list is DELETED. Gate 4N-I28AP finding ADV-I28AP-02: a prefix match skipped the approved-path membership test entirely, so any file beneath ~/.nvm/versions/node/ was accepted and the attacker's digest was recorded as the bound content. npm's identity is not a file digest — it is a CHAIN (wrapper -> symlink -> CLI JavaScript -> Node interpreter -> package root -> package.json -> installation family), and it is adjudicated by scripts/npm_authority.py, which binds the installation tree, the Node<->npm relationship and the version manager's own metadata rather than a path shape.
